title: Request for Proposal: Public Digital Experience and Intake Modernization

milestones.name: Approved experience design and solution baseline
Controlled pilot for mortgage enquiries and selected branches
Main public website and agreed intake launch

not_questions: None of the six proposed Adobe products is assumed to be licensed
RT-CDP, AJO, Workfront and Adobe Analytics are declined
Do not assume native integrations are available or sufficient
Use the client's approved accessibility, privacy, security and records policies
Distinguish included work, options, exclusions, assumptions and client responsibilities

questions.label: A.1
questions.text: Describe your proposed AEM Sites approach for deposit, mortgage enquiry and small-business journeys. Explain the content model, reusable components and author permissions, including Spanish content handling. State assumptions about page templates and provide the evidence you would use to obtain design approval by 26 March 2027.

questions.label: A.2
questions.text: Explain how you would inventory, rationalize and migrate 1,700 English pages and 140 priority Spanish pages from Drupal. Include redirect mapping, ownership decisions, missing content and migration rehearsals. Estimate effort by page complexity and propose evidence showing that every approved migration item and redirect has been reconciled.

questions.label: A.3
questions.text: Set out how branch search, product comparisons and enquiry entry points would work across mobile and desktop. Identify dependencies on branch data and approved product content. Explain how representative customers would test these journeys and demonstrate at least 90 percent completion of agreed navigation tasks without moderator assistance.

questions.label: A.4
questions.text: Propose a performance and accessibility verification plan for the public website, using bank-approved criteria and representative devices. The bank desires a two-second median largest contentful paint on agreed mobile test pages. Define network conditions, measurement windows, content responsibilities and the evidence supporting acceptance or documented exceptions.

questions.label: A.5
questions.text: Describe the publishing and rollback arrangements for AEM Sites, including scheduled rate changes and urgent branch notices. Explain how authors preview content and obtain approval before release. Demonstrate, through an agreed rehearsal, that a trained author can publish a routine notice within 15 minutes after approval.

questions.label: B.1
questions.text: Describe how AEM Assets would support the bank's 14,000 images, brochures and campaign files. Propose metadata, folder or collection arrangements, ownership and version controls. Identify licensing and configuration assumptions, and explain how a sample asset set would demonstrate that approved files can be found and reused consistently.

questions.label: B.2
questions.text: Explain your process for reviewing shared-drive files before migration, including duplicate detection, missing ownership, expired usage permissions and inaccessible documents. State which decisions remain with the bank. Provide an estimate basis for assessment and remediation, and propose reconciliation evidence covering all files selected for migration.

questions.label: B.3
questions.text: Set out the proposed process for preparing approved image variations and downloadable documents for website use. Explain where automation, manual review and author training are required. Describe a pilot in which at least 95 percent of a bank-approved sample meets the agreed naming, metadata and rendition requirements.

questions.label: B.4
questions.text: Describe how replacement, withdrawal and expiry of published assets would be controlled across the public website. Identify any dependency on delivery caching or linked documents. Explain the audit evidence and rehearsal needed to show that a withdrawn brochure is no longer served through agreed public entry points.

questions.label: C.1
questions.text: Propose an AEM Forms approach for six initial journeys covering deposit enquiries, mortgage enquiries and small-business requests. Include conditional questions, validation, document upload and accessible error handling. Explain complexity assumptions and show how agreed test cases would demonstrate accurate submission without transferring account servicing or credit decisions into scope.

questions.label: C.2
questions.text: Describe the proposed transfer of intake records and consent choices to Salesforce, including mapping, duplicate handling, failed delivery and reconciliation. Do not assume a ready-made connection meets the requirement. State interface dependencies and demonstrate through testing that every accepted submission is either delivered or visible in a recoverable exception queue.

questions.label: C.3
questions.text: Explain where Acrobat Sign is proposed for the bank's defined document journeys and how templates, signing order, reminders and completed records would be managed. Identify transaction and integration assumptions. Describe acceptance evidence for completion, refusal, expiry and retrieval, while leaving applicant identity verification with the existing external provider.

questions.label: C.4
questions.text: Set out your approach to interrupted applications and saved progress, including expiry, access controls and recovery messages. Identify what depends on the external identity provider and what requires a bank decision. Estimate the work separately where assumptions are unresolved, and propose tests that prevent one applicant from retrieving another applicant's information.

questions.label: C.5
questions.text: Provide a load and resilience test plan for 9,000 monthly submissions and 450 simultaneous intake sessions, including uploaded files and downstream delays. The bank desires 99 percent successful submissions during an agreed test. Define success, test data, duration, excluded dependencies and the evidence needed to approve pilot readiness.

questions.label: D.1
questions.text: Describe a Customer Journey Analytics design for public discovery, enquiry starts, submitted applications and signing outcomes. Explain proposed data collection and ingestion paths, supporting services and license dependencies without requiring Adobe Analytics. State how anonymous activity and permitted identifiers would be handled, with unresolved policy decisions assigned to the bank.

questions.label: D.2
questions.text: Propose a measurement specification for 18 million events monthly, including event names, required fields, consent behavior and data quality rules. Identify responsibilities for implementation and approval. Explain how testing would demonstrate at least 98 percent agreement between accepted submissions eligible under approved consent rules and corresponding measurement events under agreed reconciliation conditions.

questions.label: D.3
questions.text: Explain how relevant Salesforce outcomes and Snowflake data could support journey analysis while Power BI remains available for management reporting. Identify connection methods, refresh assumptions, transformation work and permissions. Provide a small validation exercise and estimate basis, including how missing identifiers and late-arriving records would be reported.

questions.label: D.4
questions.text: Describe the proposed dashboards and training for eight analysts and 25 business viewers. Cover enquiry conversion, abandonment, branch interest and channel comparison. Explain how definitions would be approved and demonstrate that trained analysts can reproduce five agreed reports from documented source fields without supplier assistance during acceptance.

questions.label: E.1
questions.text: Describe how Adobe Target would support controlled experiments on public product pages and enquiry entry points. Propose an initial backlog of three test types, with required implementation work and commercial dependencies. Explain how experimentation would operate without RT-CDP or AJO and how exposure would respect bank-approved consent decisions.

questions.label: E.2
questions.text: Set out the process for approving hypotheses, selecting audiences, allocating traffic and agreeing success measures before launch. Include exclusions for online banking and sensitive applicant information. Explain how insufficient traffic, overlapping campaigns and inconclusive results would be handled, and provide the evidence required for a bank owner to approve each experiment.

questions.label: E.3
questions.text: Explain how experiment exposure and outcomes would be reconciled with Customer Journey Analytics or another explicitly priced measurement approach. Identify identifier, collection and reporting dependencies without assuming a native connection is sufficient. Describe tests proving that control and variation results can be traced to the approved experiment definition.

questions.label: E.4
questions.text: Describe preview, quality assurance, release and emergency suspension procedures for experiments. The bank wants a trained operator to disable an approved test within ten minutes of an incident decision. Define the rehearsal conditions, propagation assumptions and evidence, and explain how the default experience remains usable when experimentation services are unavailable.

questions.label: F.1
questions.text: Provide a delivery plan working toward design approval on 26 March, a controlled pilot on 18 June and main launch on 24 September 2027. Show workstreams, critical dependencies, bank decisions and acceptance gates. Explain the minimum pilot scope and how licensing or procurement delays would affect sequencing and estimates.

questions.label: F.2
questions.text: Describe the environments, deployment pipeline, test data arrangements and release controls needed across the proposed products. Identify responsibilities shared with Adobe, Akamai and existing service providers. Include a cutover rehearsal, rollback criteria and launch evidence, with effort estimates distinguishing initial setup from recurring support and environment charges.

questions.label: F.3
questions.text: Propose the operating model for monitoring, incident triage, maintenance and knowledge transfer after launch. The bank requests four weeks of enhanced support and a 30-minute acknowledgement target for critical incidents during agreed coverage hours. Define those hours, escalation dependencies, exclusions and evidence from an operational readiness exercise.

questions.label: F.4
questions.text: Provide the basis for a phased implementation estimate and a three-year operating cost view. Separate product subscriptions, integrations, migration, testing, training and support. State quantities, rates, client effort and uncertainty ranges, and describe how discovery findings, additional forms or deferred acceptance decisions would change scope through agreed change control.

questions.label: G.1
questions.section: G Supplier capability and commercial approach
questions.text: Describe your proposed team, named delivery leadership and relevant experience with comparable public digital and intake projects. Distinguish employee and subcontractor responsibilities, availability and product-specific experience. Provide two references or anonymized examples where permission limits disclosure, explaining which delivery outcomes can be independently evidenced and which remain self-reported.

questions.label: G.2
questions.section: G Supplier capability and commercial approach
questions.text: Explain how your team would work with the bank's marketing, technology, security and operations staff, including expected weekly commitments and decision turnaround. Describe how specialist gaps and staff changes would be managed. State which client contributions are essential to your estimate and how unresolved dependencies would be escalated.

questions.label: G.3
questions.section: G Supplier capability and commercial approach
questions.text: Describe your proposed commercial structure, payment milestones, proposal validity and treatment of third-party charges. Identify exclusions, optional services and assumptions that materially affect price. Explain how the bank could compare the base proposal with separately priced options, and how deliverable acceptance would be evidenced before a milestone invoice.

questions.label: H.1
questions.text: Describe the proposed handling of personal information across collection, transmission, storage, analysis and deletion. Identify data locations, subprocessors and decisions requiring bank approval. Explain how a documented data flow and representative deletion test would be reviewed, using supplied bank policies without asserting that a product or implementation guarantees regulatory compliance.

questions.label: H.2
questions.text: Set out how administrative access, service credentials and audit records would be managed across the proposed solution. Distinguish workforce access from applicant identity services retained externally. Identify dependencies and propose evidence from access reviews, credential rotation and unauthorized-access tests, including how findings would be tracked to an agreed owner.

questions.label: H.3
questions.text: Describe your security testing and remediation approach before pilot and main launch, including responsibility for third-party testing and supplier coordination. The bank requires no unresolved findings it classifies as critical at launch. Explain classification review, retesting evidence, exception approval and how remediation effort is reflected in your estimate.
